name: Autosomal Dominant Intermediate Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for CMT

criteria.description: Presence of autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected family members
Nerve conduction studies showing intermediate conduction velocities (25-45 m/s)
Symmetrical distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting lower limbs
Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes such as GJB1, MPZ, or MFN2
Nerve biopsy showing intermediate demyelination and axonal loss

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of autosomal dominant inheritance, characteristic clinical features, and electrophysiological evidence of intermediate nerve conduction velocities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and electrophysiological criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Symmetrical distal muscle weakness and atrophy
searchTerms: muscle weakness and wasting in hands and feet
symmetrical muscle loss in distal limbs
weakness and shrinkage of distal muscles

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intermediate nerve conduction velocity slowing (25-45 m/s)

common.symptomName: Distal sensory loss in lower limbs
searchTerms: loss of feeling in lower feet and legs
reduced sensation in feet and legs

common.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes

occasional.symptomName: Mild distal sensory loss in upper limbs

searchTerms: difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Elevated creatine kinase may be mild or absent
imaging: MRI may show muscle atrophy in distal limbs
Nerve ultrasound may show nerve enlargement
genetic: Mutations in GJB1 (Connexin 32), MPZ, MFN2 genes
other: Nerve conduction studies showing intermediate slowing
Nerve biopsy with mixed demyelinating and axonal features

distinguishingFeatures: Markedly slowed nerve conduction velocities (< 38 m/s)
Normal or mildly reduced nerve conduction velocities (> 38 m/s)

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness or sensory loss
references: Pareyson D, Marchesi C. Diagnosis, natural history, and management of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Lancet Neurol. 2009;8(7):654-667.
